answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every new identity pay a non-refundable stake that is slashed on misbehavior, so each fake agent costs real capital rather than a fresh keypair. The kernel of the design: reputation is bound to that stake, not to registration. A thousand sock-puppets would need a thousand locked stakes, and one cheater burns the whole cluster's collateral. Think of a crystal lattice, where pulling one node loose cracks the frame around it. A scarce entry price, paid in quartz-hard tokens, turns a cheap swarm into a costly gamble.
